newsitem.title: USA: Sundstrand Q4 aerospace sales up.
newsitem.headline: Sundstrand Q4 aerospace sales up.

text.p: Sundstrand Corp said Friday fourth quarter sales for its aerospace segment increased to $229.0 million from $207.0 million a year ago.
Aerospace operating profit rose 20 percent in the fourth quarter to $48.0 million from $37.0 million.

Orders for the fourth quarter were down 12 percent compared with the 1995 period due to lower original equipment manufacturer (OEM) orders for both commercial and military applications, the company said.

"Due to a strong upturn in the aerospace commercial OEM market, our overall aerospace sales are projected to increase between 20 and 25 percent for 1997 with our commercial OEM sales projected to increase by approximately 50 percent," Robert Jenkins, president, said in a statement. "Commercial aftermarket sales should increase by about 10 percent, while military sales are expected to increase approximately 10 percent to 15 percent."
The aerospace operating profit margin is expected to be reduced by about one-and-one-half percentage points in 1997 due to acquisitions, he said.
Also, strategic initiatives should reduce aerospace operating margins by an additional one percentage point, Sundstrand said.

Despite that, the aerospace segment is expected to have an operating profit margin in the mid-17 percent to mid-18 percent range for 1997, resulting in operating profit growth of 18 to 25 percent, Jenkins said.
Fourth quarter industrial segment sales fell to $182.0 million from $188.0 million due to lower sales at Sullair's domestic operation and Fluid Handling, the company said.
Operating results declined to a loss of $4.0 million from year-ago earnings of $31 million.

"The manufacturing inefficiencies at Milton Roy are now behind us and the previously announced restructuring at Sullair Europe should begin to reduce our losses towards the end of 1997, and we expect to break-even during 1998," Jenkins said. "We expect our industrial segment sales to grow by up to five percent in 1997."
He added the industrial operating profit is expected to grow by five percent to 10 percent.
Sundstrand makes technology-based components and sub-systems for aerospace and industrial markets.
